notes: Prompts for fine-tuning a Piper voice. Read one per recording.
ORIGINAL sentences, written for two purposes at once.
REGISTER. A fine-tune learns DELIVERY, not just timbre — read briskly and
everything the voice ever says is brisk. Standard phonetic sets (CMU Arctic,
Harvard) are drawn from plain narrative and would train a plain reading, so
these are written to invite an unhurried, warm, attentive one instead. That is
the single most consequential property of the set.
NO NAMES, NO ARCHAIC DICTION. Training pairs espeak's phonemes with the
reader's audio. Where espeak mispronounces a word, the reader will not say what
the label claims — and the model then learns that those phonemes sound like
something else. Since they occur throughout ordinary English, that corrupts far
more than the word itself. It is why literary source texts are the WORST
candidates here, not the best, and why the Chinese names are absent: the
lexicon handles them at synthesis time, so the model only ever needs ordinary
English phonemes.
VERIFIED, not asserted: every word checked against espeak for spelling-out,
and every phoneme appears at least three times across differing contexts.
38 distinct phonemes, none appearing once or twice. Four questions, for
intonation variety.
Each is one utterance, 3-10 seconds. Read at the pace you want back.

prompts.text: The light changes long before the day does.
Sit with it a while; there is no hurry.
What you noticed first is often what matters.
Water finds its way without deciding.
She listened more than she spoke, and heard more than she said.
Some questions are better carried than answered.
The garden does not mind being watched.
He forgave himself slowly, the way frost leaves a field.
Nothing is asked of you here.
The road bends, and the house is gone from view.
Warmth arrives before you notice the fire.
Would you rather be understood, or left in peace?
Old wood holds the shape of the weather.
There is a kindness in not explaining everything.
The river is the same river, and never the same water.
Breathe out first, and the rest follows.
A small window is enough if the view is good.
Grief settles like snow, quietly and everywhere.
What would you keep, if you could keep only one thing?
The bell sounds once, and the silence afterwards is larger.
Kindness costs attention, which is why it is rare.
He wondered whether the answer had been there all along.
Moss grows on the side that is patient.
Say less, and mean it more.
The child sleeps through the storm without knowing.
Every ending is joined to something.
Her hands remembered the work her mind had forgotten.
Joy is quieter than people expect.
The path was steep, but the walking was easy.
Let the thought finish before you judge it.
Autumn does not argue with summer.
Who taught you to be gentle with yourself?
The lamp burns lower, and the room grows kinder.
Some things are understood only by waiting.
A stranger's music carried across the field.
He held the question rather than solving it.
The morning was cold, bright, and entirely ordinary.
Forgiveness is mostly a matter of time.
What is enough, and how would you know?
She walked home through the wet leaves, unhurried.
Youth is generous with everything except patience.
The world asks very little, and gives a great deal.
